body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to the Omniscient One.

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutamekasmin samaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārddhaṃ trayodaśabhirbhikṣuśataiḥ / tatra khalu bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma -
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavān</s>) was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s> grove, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), thirteen hundred <s>bhikṣus</s>. There the Blessed One addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s>:

body.text: anityā bhikṣavaḥ sarvasaṃskārā adhruvā anāsvāsikā vipariṇāmadharmāṇaḥ / yadyāvat bhikṣavaḥ sarvebhyaḥ saṃskārebhyo 'laṃ nirvartitumalaṃ viraktamalaṃ vimoktum / sarveṣāṃ sattvānāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ āmaraṇānta hi jīvita maraṇa paryavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇam /
body.translated_text: "O <s>bhikṣus</s>, all <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations) are impermanent, unstable, unreliable, and subject to change. Indeed, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, one should turn away from all <s>saṃskāras</s>, one should become dispassionate toward them, one should become liberated from them. For all beings, for all creatures, for all living things, life ends in death, life has death as its conclusion — there is no deathlessness for one who has been born.

body.text: yepi te bhikṣavo gṛhapatayo mahāśālakulā brāhmaṇa mahāśālakulākṣatriya mahāśālakulā āśāṃ mahādhano mahābhogāḥ prabhūtamaṇimāṇikyamuktāvaiduryaśaṃkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajatavikaraṇāḥ prabhūtadhanadhānyakoṣakoṣṭhāgārasannicayāḥ prabhūtadāsīdāsakarmakara paurūṣeyo prabhūtamitrāmātyajñātisālohitāsteṣāmapi maraṇāntaṃ jīvitamaraṇaṃparyavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: O <s>bhikṣus</s>, even those householders of great and wealthy <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families, of great and wealthy <s>kṣatriya</s> families — those of great wealth, of great possessions, possessing abundant gems, jewels, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), conch-shells, crystal, coral, gold, silver, and ornaments, possessing abundant stores of wealth, grain, treasuries, and granaries, possessing abundant male and female servants, workers, and attendants, possessing abundant friends, ministers, relatives, and kinsmen — even for them, life ends in death, life has death as its conclusion; there is no deathlessness for one who has been born.

body.text: yepi te bhikṣavaḥ rājānaḥ kṣatriyāśca murddhābhiṣiktā jānapadai śvaryasthāmavīryamanuprāptā mahāntaṃ pṛthvīmaṇḍalamabhinirjityā vasanti / teṣāmapi maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitaṃ maraṇaparyavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: O <s>bhikṣus</s>, even those kings, <s>kṣatriyas</s> anointed upon the head, who have attained the sovereignty, power, strength, and might over their realms, who dwell having conquered a great territory of the earth — even for them, life ends in death, life has death as its conclusion; there is no deathlessness for one who has been born.

body.text: yepi te bhikṣavaḥ ṛṣayo vānaprasthāḥ pramukta phalāhārāḥ prabhūktaphala bhojinaḥ pramukta phalena yāpanti teṣāmapi maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvita maraṇaparyavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: O <s>bhikṣus</s>, even those <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages), forest-dwelling ascetics (<s>vānaprasthas</s>), who subsist on roots and fruits, who eat fruits, who sustain themselves on roots and fruits — even for them, life ends in death, life has death as its conclusion; there is no deathlessness for one who has been born.

body.text: yepi te bhikṣavaḥ kāmāvacāradevāścāturmahārājikādevāstrayāstriśāṃdevānāmāstuṣitādevānirmāṇaratayodevāḥ paranirmitavaśavartinodevāsteṣāmapi maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitaṃ maraṇa paryavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: O <s>bhikṣus</s>, even those gods of the desire realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>) — the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, the gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods — even for them, life ends in death, life has death as its conclusion; there is no deathlessness for one who has been born.

body.text: yepi te bhikṣavo rūpiṇo devāḥ prathamadhyānalābhino brahmakāyikā brahmapurohitā mahābrahmāṇaḥ dvitīya dhyānalābhina parītābhā apramāṇābhā ābhāśvarā stṛtīyadhyāna lābhinaḥparītaśubhā apramāṇaśubhā śubhakṛtsnā caturthadhyāna lābhinonabhrakā puṇyaprasavā bṛhatphalā avṛhā atapā sudṛśāḥ sudarśanā akaniṣṭhāścadevāsteṣāmapi maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ paryavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇaṃ /
body.translated_text: O <s>bhikṣus</s>, even those gods possessing form (<s>rūpin</s>) — those who have attained the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation): the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, and <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods; those who have attained the second <s>dhyāna</s>: the <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, and <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods; those who have attained the third <s>dhyāna</s>: the <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, and <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods; those who have attained the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>: the <s>Anabhrakā</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Avṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśā</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods — even for them, life ends in death, life has death as its conclusion; there is no deathlessness for one who has been born.

body.text: yepi te bhikṣavaḥ ārūpiṇodevā ākāśānantaāyatanopagā vijñānantyāyatanopagā ākiṃcanyāyatanopagā naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanopagāśca devāsteṣāmapi maraṇāntahi jīvita maraṇaṃ paryavasāna nāsti jātasyāmaraṇa / traidhātukamidaṃ /
body.translated_text: O <s>bhikṣus</s>, even those formless gods (<s>ārūpin</s>) — those who have attained the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>), the sphere of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>), the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>), and the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>) — even for them, life ends in death, life has death as its conclusion; there is no deathlessness for one who has been born. This is the triple realm (<s>traidhātuka</s>).

body.text: yepi te bhikṣavo 'rhantaḥ kṣīṇāsravā kṛtakṛtyāḥ kṛtakaraṇīyā apahṛtabhārā anuprāptatvākāthā parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittāḥ sarvacetovaśiparamapāramitāprāptāsteṣāmapi kāyanikṣepaṇadharmāḥ /
body.translated_text: O <s>bhikṣus</s>, even those <s>Arhats</s> whose defilements are exhausted (<s>kṣīṇāsrava</s>), who have done what was to be done, who have accomplished their task, who have laid down the burden, who have attained their own goal, who have completely destroyed the fetters of existence (<s>bhavasaṃyojana</s>), who are liberated in mind through right knowledge, who have reached the supreme perfection of complete mastery over all minds — even for them, the nature of this body is to be cast off.

body.text: yepi te bhikṣavaḥ pratyekabuddhā khaḍga viṣāṇakalpā ekamātmāna damayanti ekamātmāna śamayati ekamātmātmānaṃparinirvāyanti teṣāmapi 'yaṃkāyonikṣepaṇadharmaḥ /
body.translated_text: O <s>bhikṣus</s>, even those <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), like the horn of a rhinoceros, who tame themselves alone, who calm themselves alone, who attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> by themselves alone — even for them, the nature of this body is to be cast off.

body.text: yepi te bhikṣavastathāgatā arhantaḥ samyak saṃbuddhādaśavalavalinaḥudārārṣamāḥsamyak siṃhanādanādineścaturvaiśāradyadharmārohaṇa vaiśāradyaṃ / sarvadharmadeśanāvaiśāradyaṃ nirvāṇamārgavatāraṇavaiśāradyaṃ āśravajñāna prahāṇāvaiśāradyaṃ / viśadādṛḍhanārāyaṇasaṃhatakāyāsteṣāmapyayaṃkāyonikṣepaṇa dharmaḥ / tadyathāpi nāma bhikṣavaḥ kumbhakārakṛtāni bhāṇḍāniśrāmānivāpakvāni va bhedanaparyantāni bhedana paryavasānānyevameva bhikṣavaḥ sarveṣāṃ sattvānāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇināṃ āmaraṇāntaṃ hi jīvita maraṇaparyavasānaṃ nāsti jātasyāmaraṇaṃ / īdamavocadbhagavānnidamukto sugato hyathā parovāca śāstā /
body.translated_text: O <s>bhikṣus</s>, even those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, endowed with the ten powers, who roar the great lion's roar of sages — possessing the four kinds of <s>vaiśāradya</s> (fearlessness): fearlessness in teaching all <s>dharmas</s>, fearlessness in proclaiming the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, fearlessness in the knowledge of the destruction of <s>āśravas</s> (defilements), and complete fearlessness — whose bodies are clear, firm, and compact like <s>Nārāyaṇa's</s> — even their bodies are subject to the nature of being cast aside. O <s>bhikṣus</s>, just as vessels made by a potter, whether raw or fired, all end in breaking and have breaking as their final destiny, even so, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, the life of all beings, all creatures, all living things has death as its limit and ends in death. There is no deathlessness for one who is born. This is what the Blessed One said. Having said this, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), the Teacher, further spoke:

children.translated_text: Impermanent indeed are <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned things), subject to the law of arising and passing away;
having arisen, they cease — their pacification is happiness.
Just as a vessel of clay made by a potter
all ends in breaking, so too is the life of beings.
Just as for ripe fruits there is always the fear of falling,

children.text: tathā saṃskārajāḥ satvā nityaṃ maraṇato bhayaṃ //
children.translated_text: so for beings born of <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned existence) there is always the fear of death.
All accumulations end in exhaustion, all that rises high ends in falling,
all unions end in separation, and life ends in death.

body.text: idamavocad bhagavānāttamanāste ca bhikṣavaḥ sā ca parṣadobhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan /
body.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Delighted, those <s>bhikṣus</s> and that entire assembly rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.
Thus concludes the <s>Āryānityatāsūtra</s> (Noble Sūtra on Impermanence).
